class.name: NetwSpawnBook
class.brief_description: One session's spawn ledger: what is armed, what was issued, and what this peer materialized.
class.description: The issued book answers in the order the session armed its spawns, which is stable and reproducible. That order is NOT ancestry order: a reparent can move an entity under a parent armed after it, so anything that reads a parent's answer before a child's iterates [method ancestry_order] instead. A route is enrolled in the received book before its node is placed, so a locally applied spawn can never re-arm the route it just materialized. [codeblock] arm / take_armed the verb ran, the node is still orphaned issue / spawned_of the SPAWN went out, and this is the replay book enroll_recv / is_recv this peer materialized the route from the server [/codeblock] Every record holds its node as an id, so a node freed while armed drops out of [method armed_records] answers rather than dangling. See [NetwSpawnRecord].

method.name: despawn_order
method.description: [param route] and every issued route beneath it, ordered CHILDREN BEFORE the ancestor that contains them, which is [method ancestry_order] read backwards over that subtree alone. A receiver has to process a child's despawn before the ancestor's, for the same reason a spawn goes parent-first read backwards. The whole order is answered before the first drop, so a caller iterating it is not reading a book it is mutating. A [param route] the book never issued answers empty, and a sibling subtree is never carried along.

method.name: ancestry_order
method.description: Every issued route with each one after its [member NetwSpawnRecord.parent_route]. Ancestry is the order a per-peer verdict has to be read in, because a child's verdict is clamped by its parent's.

method.name: arm
method.description: Arms [param record] under its own [member NetwSpawnRecord.route]. A record is its own key, so an armed route and the record's route can never name different spawns.

method.name: armed_count
method.description: How many spawns are armed and not yet placed.

method.name: armed_records
method.description: Every armed record, in arm order.

method.name: clear
method.description: Drops all three books. A node still armed is reported, because reaching here with one means a replicated node was never placed in the tree.

method.name: drop_armed
method.description: Forgets an armed route without taking its record, and answers whether it was there.

method.name: drop_recv
method.description: Forgets a materialized route, and answers whether it was there.

method.name: drop_spawned
method.description: Drops an issued route from the replay book, and answers whether it was there.

method.name: enroll_recv
method.description: Claims [param route] for a node this peer materialized from the server. It runs before the node is placed, so the route is claimed while the node is still orphaned and a locally applied spawn can never re-arm it.

method.name: has_armed
method.description: Whether [param route] is armed and not yet placed.

method.name: has_spawned
method.description: Whether [param route] was issued from here.

method.name: is_recv
method.description: Whether [param route] was materialized on this peer from the server.

method.name: issue
method.description: Records that [param record]'s spawn went out, under the same key [method arm] used.

method.name: recv_count
method.description: How many routes this peer materialized from the server.

method.name: spawned_count
method.description: How many spawns this peer has issued.

method.name: recipe_base
method.description: The stem an auto-assigned entity id is built from: the scene's basename for [constant RECIPE_SCENE], the spawn function's name for [constant RECIPE_FN], the registered id for [constant RECIPE_FN_REGISTRY]. Every other recipe has no stem of its own, so it falls to [param fallback_scene_path]'s basename and then to [param fallback_name], which are the spawning node's own scene and name. A null [param record] takes the same fallback, because an id still has to be assignable when the record is gone.

method.name: parent_admits
method.description: Whether [param route]'s issued parent already counts [param peer] among its recipients, which is the clamp a spawn owes: a peer that receives a child before its parent has nowhere to put it. This reads the MATERIALIZED recipients rather than the desired ones, so it answers "may this be sent now" rather than "should this be there at all". A route with no parent, a route whose parent the book does not hold, and a route the book never issued are all UNCLAMPED, because a clamp against an absent parent would strand a record nothing can ever release.

method.name: spawn_is_duplicate
method.description: Whether an arriving spawn for [param route] is one this peer already stood up. True where the book already enrolled a received node for the route, and true where [param state] is [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LIVE] or [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LINGERING]. A [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_DEAD] route is NOT a duplicate, and that is the whole reason this is a verb rather than a comparison. Spawn and despawn share one reliable ordered channel, so a spawn arriving after the despawn that tombstoned a route is an interest RE-ADMISSION reviving the entity, never a stale packet. Reading DEAD as "already handled" drops the revival and the entity never comes back.

method.name: spawned_of
method.description: The issued record for [param route], or [code]null[/code].

method.name: spawned_records
method.description: Every issued record, in arm order.

method.name: spawned_routes
method.description: Every issued route, in arm order. It is a copy, so a caller may drop routes while walking it.

constants.constant: The node reconstructs by instantiating its [member Node.scene_file_path].
The node reconstructs by invoking a spawn function on a host object that exists on every peer.
The node reconstructs through a [MultiplayerSpawner], addressed by anchor with the spawner's own scene-index compression.
The node is not reconstructed at all: every peer already holds it at the frame's parent anchor and name, and the frame only stamps identity onto the existing instance.
The node reconstructs by invoking a spawn function the session registered under a stable id, resolved from the id alone with no host node.
